bug_info.bug_desc: The cache-line bit offset discards address bit 2 and advances in 64-bit units. With XLEN=32, addresses in the upper 32-bit word of each 64-bit block therefore use the preceding word's cache-line position. This affects both cache-hit reads and byte-enabled cache-hit writes.
bug_info.fix_hint: Compute the cache-line bit offset from the address using XLEN-sized words.

bug_info.bug_desc: The outgoing miss or bypass request copies the core byte enables into the low bus lanes regardless of the request address. With XLEN=32 on the 64-bit memory interface, an upper-word store consequently enables the wrong bytes.
bug_info.fix_hint: Position the core byte enables within the 64-bit request according to the saved address and XLEN.

bug_info.bug_desc: The outgoing miss or bypass request copies the core write data into the low bits of the 64-bit bus word regardless of the request address. With XLEN=32, an upper-word store has incorrect data at the addressed bus lanes even if its byte enables are aligned.
bug_info.fix_hint: Position the core write data in the addressed XLEN word of the memory-side request.

bug_info.bug_desc: The refill load response assigns the entire 64-bit critical word to the XLEN-bit core result. With XLEN=32 this always retains the low 32 bits, including when the saved address requests the upper word.
bug_info.fix_hint: Select the addressed XLEN word from the critical-word response before returning it to the core.

bug_info.bug_desc: The bypass load response assigns the entire 64-bit bypass data to the XLEN-bit core result. With XLEN=32 this always retains the low 32 bits, including when the saved address requests the upper word.
bug_info.fix_hint: Select the addressed XLEN word from the bypass response before returning it to the core.
